headline: Highest risk is medium: Superset can ingest AI-engineering-hub outputs via shared APIs/workflows, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct evidence of shared storage or secrets handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a is an AI/agents hub with MCP/RAG tags, so it may emit instruction-like content; agent_b exposes a Superset API and is a data-engineering app that can consume external inputs. No shared channel is documented, so the pathway is inferred rather than proven, but uncertainty should escalate above low.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs content that operator pastes into agent_b workflows or API payloads
IF agent_b parses imported text or metadata as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste bridge between the two agents
Require a human review step before importing agent_a output into Superset
Strip markdown/code blocks from agent_a outputs before reuse
Use a separate staging workspace for any transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a reports network_egress:none and no data classes touched; agent_b has allowlisted egress but also no data classes touched and no shared workspace, OAuth, or secrets are documented. With no evidence of sensitive data flow between them, a leakage pathway is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are later connected to the same workspace containing sensitive files
IF agent_b is configured to ingest files produced by agent_a
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not place secrets in any shared directory
Review Superset import sources before enabling them

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no documented write surfaces and agent_b only exposes Superset API calls, so direct write-write conflict is not shown. A conflict could still arise if both are wired to the same mutable Superset resources, but that requires unusual orchestration and the profiles do not prove overlapping writes.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same Superset objects
IF an orchestrator routes concurrent updates without locking
mitigations: Use separate API tokens per workflow
Add a manual approval step before writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate agentic/RAG content, and agent_b can act on API-driven inputs in a BI workflow. If Superset consumes agent_a output as authoritative, errors can cascade into dashboards or downstream decisions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a source of truth
IF no validation or reconciliation step is inserted before Superset actions
mitigations: Require source citations for any transferred facts
Compare agent_a output against original data before use
Limit agent_b to read-only operations until reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile documents regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies. Because compliance risk depends on a specific data class or jurisdictional flow that is absent here, no concrete compliance breach is established for this pair.
conditions: IF EU PII or PHI is later introduced into either agent
IF retention or residency policies differ for the same data class
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through either agent
Add retention and residency checks in the workflow
